Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation; fixing 99 negatives ensures comparable comparisons but does not remove sampling bias ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Interpret this benchmark’s HR@10 strictly as performance on its pinned candidate distribution. Recommended controls: training-only item popularity, a smoothed last-item transition model with popularity fallback, and an order-insensitive history model. Compare SASRec with shuffled-history variants while preserving targets and splits. Published sequential-data analysis uses this shuffle control with matched random seeds ([An Analysis of Sequential Recommendation Datasets](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-2955/paper8.pdf)). Shuffling at inference measures sensitivity to order; retraining on shuffled histories better tests whether learning order contributes. Neither alone proves useful long-range dependencies.

For this benchmark, recommended uncertainty analysis: retain each user’s binary hit for every model; bootstrap users with replacement separately within each category, using identical resampled users for both models, then average the four category-level HR differences. Report the observed difference, paired 95% interval, and category results. Keep candidates fixed: the interval is conditional on those candidates and trained checkpoints, excluding negative-sampling and training-seed variability. Bootstrap and randomization tests have empirical support in recommendation evaluation ([Ihemelandu and Ekstrand](https://piret.info/pubs/2023/SIGIR23-InferenceAtScale)).

Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can overfit validation noise ([Cawley and Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). A bootstrap interval around the selected winner does not correct adaptive selection. Log every attempted configuration, predeclare controls and the search budget, and treat validation intervals as descriptive. Freeze the chosen configuration before the host’s independent held-out evaluation; do not alter the evaluator, splits, or candidates.
